items.rationale: The bicycle was recovered undamaged, so §§2.3.3 and 7.1.8(c) exclude the entire elective swap, not just the premium over a standard frame.
Under §§3.1.6 and 7.1.10, renewing brakes during routine service is maintenance, not repair of theft damage.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.8(a) exclude routine servicing and tuning; no theft damage to the drivetrain was established.
Under §7.1.10, shipping on the elective service invoice follows the excluded work. Nothing identifies it as transport from the recovery site under §5.2.2(d).
Section 7.1.8(f) excludes attendance charges on an invoice with no covered work; the recovery attendance is separately billed by the locksmith.
Under §§7.1.8(a) and 7.1.10, assembly follows the elective upgrade and service it supports, not a covered repair.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.10 exclude labour of every grade when it serves elective work on an undamaged bicycle.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.10 exclude this hour because it serves the elective upgrade and maintenance, not recovery or theft repair.

Section 5.2.2(a) covers the necessary attendance even though the bicycle was recovered undamaged. Estimated covered recovery costs of €199 in total are below the €500 aggregate mobility limit, so no proration applies.

items.description: Cut and remove seized lock, two units
items.rationale: Section 5.2.2(b) covers the necessary lock removal. At €60 per billed unit, the whole line is €120, assuming the operation charge does not duplicate the separately billed labour (§7.1.8(g)).
Section 5.2.2(b) covers necessary labour to release the bicycle; one hour is estimated at €39 gross if not already included in the cutting charge (§7.1.8(g)).
